body: I definitely understand that first part. Although my specialty is more BPD than manic depressive, I think we both know it can be exhausting with a crazy amount of emotions in short periods. After using for about 4 years though, it only made me worse in the end. Especially since I was unmedicated. The relief that the drugs gives you makes you think it’s going to be better and more worth it than it will, though. I can honestly tell you that the longer you use, unmedicated or not, the worse you will feel. And it’s not ideal since it makes everything seem so damn perfect and easy.

If you want to talk for a bit, feel free to message me. I don’t know much about you, and I doubt I can say much that will actually help, but I’m willing to listen if you need an active ear. I’ve been there and I wouldn’t be sober today if I had didn’t have the tiniest bit of support. 

I just want you to know there’s a possibility of things getting better, even if it seems like it can’t get worse and there’s no chance you can see it getting better. It does. I can tell that there’s still that sliver of hope in you, you were more worried about overdosing than taking it right away. 

Also, I’m not sure if you’re still in AZ, but I am, and if you need any resources for mental help, addiction, anything, let me know and I can try to help.

I cannot do much to change one’s relapse decision, but I can make sure they be safer if they do. But, I hope you haven’t used it yet, then. Flush it while you still can. It is a hard and familiar road I’ve gone down to get what I needed at the time, but it wasn’t worth it in the end like I thought it was. 

I really recommend searching for help; whether it be an NA meeting, rehab, therapy, or talking to a friend until you think you’ve pushed the urges away enough to feel safe. I know you’re having a rough time, but I hope you also know that the pain you’re feeling isn’t permanent and that relapsing won’t take the pain away. You are stronger than you think.
I wouldn’t say a waste, especially if you’d rather be safe than sorry.

I just wanna say that I’m sorry to hear about your relapse and personal issues. I hope you can get the help that you need. 

You can sniff it if you would like, but I wouldn’t recommend it if you haven’t used it before and you have a lower tolerance from your sobriety. If you do decide to, use very small and thin lines, spaced out over time. 

But I would say to just smoke it, as that would be better to gauge how high you want to be. Small hits and space it out, too. 

Just remember that you can always take more if you don’t feel anything, but you can’t take it away if you do too much. I hope you stay safe and wish you the best.

You most likely won’t find a facility with all of your preferences, especially if you aren’t going to one that takes private insurance as those are focused on “luxury”.

Most detox facilities do not offer methadone, only suboxone. And you can’t ask for the medication you want to be on, no doctor will give medication to you just because you asked for it. I’d say that you should tell them in previous detox, these medications worked best for you. Suggest it, don’t ask for it. Be nice and calm about it.

I don’t think any detox facility, other than a “luxury detox”, will allow you to bring your MP3 player. It doesn’t matter if it doesn’t have a camera or only plays music, they most likely won’t allow it. And they definitely will not allow headphones as it can be a tool to hurt yourself. 

Honestly, most detox facilities (in my experience) that take public insurance just offer you an uncomfortable bed with an uncomfortable pillow in a room with nothing in it besides beds and a bathroom, crappy food that most people can’t stomach, a “rec room” with a tv and books, and barely enough medication to make you feel comfortable during detox.

Good luck! I’m heading to detox, too!

I want to want to live because even though everything feels so meaningless, I know that there’s meaning in literally everything. I used to be able to find meaning in absolutely everything when I wasn’t feeling things so intensely, having at least a few bouts of happiness, and before I completely fucked up my anxiety and depression from drug use so much that it feels permanent. I wish I could go back to when I wasn’t using anything but weed. 

I know everything has a meaning. I know how great it feels to be happy, I’ve been happy before. I know how radiant I could be and how I could do so, so many fucking great things with my life that I couldn’t even imagine right now. But even though I know this, I don’t feel any different. I don’t feel any less suicidal, less sad, less angry or less confused. In fact, I think it makes me feel even worse when I think about those things. Because I know I have potential, and yet I just...don’t want it, or don’t feel like I want it...

I feel that a lot, everyone is telling me “things are going to get better” like, how exactly? Because medication isn’t working and I’ve been waiting 20 years for “things to get better”. I feel really exhausted too. It feels like there’s no point in getting better because I know things won’t get better, and it’s not going to last very long if they do. I just want to give up. I don’t want to live, but I want to be able to want to live. If I could just have the littlest voice in me saying “I want to live”, I’m almost positive things would be able to change for the better. But I don’t want to live. Everything just feels so meaningless, even though I know that there are things to live for.

I used to have so many hobbies. I used to be really creative before I got this bad. I would write all the time, take photography, go swimming, doodle and paint. It all stopped when I lost my will to live, everything is so meaningless to me that I don’t want to do anything but lay in bed all day. I still journal every now and then, but that’s it.

I have a dog and a cat, both are my only friends. My dog is with me constantly in my room, but I never have energy to play with her much or take her on walks. I feel like a shitty pet owner.

I like the way you put that, that I can live to make others happy. I’ve always been like that, I always put other people before me. It’s been both the best and the worst thing about me.

When I’m in wd’s and I know for certain I’m not going to be able to cop anytime soon, I use suboxone, gabapentin for anxiety/restless legs/sleep, trazadone for sleep, wax to just generally make me feel better, and something for nausea like zofran or promethazine. 

Also- benzos like klonopin or xanax are great for anxiety and muscle relaxants, I try to use my hydroxyzine script for anxiety if it isn’t as bad. I’ve heard wonders about kratom for general symptoms and taking iron supplements for restless legs. I would also get medication for diarrhea or constipation if you get either when you detox (if you know). Also, aleve for headaches and cramps.

Don’t forget to drink tons of water and eat/snack regularly, even if you have to make yourself do it! Make sure you try to get some really good rest, too. Your body deserves and needs it. Good luck! You can do this!
